Chemical Agent Instructor Course

A 40-hour, California POST-certified instructor course that prepares officers to teach, deploy and document chemical agents safely, lawfully and effectively.

  • Review of use of force and related agency policies
  • Deployment techniques and munition selection
  • Use of the protective mask
  • Use of chemical agent munitions
  • Decontamination and aftercare
  • Instruction techniques and lesson-plan development
  • Scenario exercises — including AB 48 / PC 13652 requirements

$1,881 tuition per student · POST Plan IV reimbursable

How long is the Chemical Agent Instructor Course?

It is a 40-hour, instructor-level course combining classroom instruction, practical deployment work and scenario exercises.

Is the course POST certified and reimbursable?

Yes. The course is California POST certified and listed as Plan IV reimbursable, which covers tuition. Travel and per diem are not reimbursed under Plan IV — confirm eligibility with your agency training manager.

item.title: AB 48 Compliance Training
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
What Is AB 48?

Assembly Bill 48 (2021) added Section 13652 to the California Penal Code, effective January 1, 2022. It restricts how law enforcement agencies may use kinetic energy projectiles and chemical agents to disperse an assembly, protest or demonstration — and it ties lawful use directly to training.

Under PC 13652, only officers who have received POST-standard training in crowd-control use may deploy these tools in those situations.

[sws_notice title="AB 48 — Certifications Prior to January 2022"]California Assembly Bill 48 states that any kinetic energy projectiles and chemical agents shall only be deployed by a peace officer that has received training on their proper use by the Commission on Peace Officer Standards and Training (POST), starting January 2022. All previous certifications prior to January 2022 have been de-certified. Southwestern Solutions Chemical Agent and Less Lethal Instructor Courses meet AB 48 requirements and are POST certified.[/sws_notice]

The Core Requirements

Under PC 13652, kinetic energy projectiles and chemical agents may be used in crowd situations only when objectively reasonable to defend against a threat to life or serious bodily injury, or to bring an objectively dangerous and unlawful situation safely and effectively under control — and only in accordance with conditions that include:

  • Attempting de-escalation and other reasonable alternatives when objectively reasonable.
  • Repeated, audible announcements of the intent to use these tools and the type to be used, in a manner and languages likely to be understood, when objectively reasonable.
  • Reasonable efforts to distinguish individuals engaged in violent acts from those who are not, and targeting only those engaged in violent acts.
  • Providing an objectively reasonable opportunity to disperse and leave the scene.
  • Never aiming kinetic energy projectiles at the head, neck or other vital organs.
  • Not deploying solely because of a curfew violation, a verbal threat or noncompliance with a directive.
  • Ensuring medical aid is available or summoned after deployment.

Reporting Obligations

AB 48 also requires agencies to publish on their websites a summary of each incident in which these tools were used to disperse a crowd (Penal Code 13652.1). Accurate documentation starts in training.

How Southwestern Solutions Helps

  • Our Chemical Agent Instructor Course teaches AB 48 / PC 13652 directly inside its 40-hour curriculum.
  • Our Less Lethal Instructor Course covers AB 48 requirements and compliance throughout its 30 hours.
  • Graduates return with lesson plans, drills and documentation practices that support your agency's policy and reporting.
[sws_cta title="Make AB 48 Compliance Second Nature" text="Certify instructors who can teach the law, the tactics and the documentation as one system." button="View Courses" url="/courses/"]

This summary is for training and educational purposes only and is not legal advice. Refer to the full text of California Penal Code sections 13652 and 13652.1, current POST guidelines and your agency's legal counsel.

item.title: Frequently Asked Questions
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
[sws_section eyebrow="Answers" title="Common Questions"]
How long is the Chemical Agent Instructor Course?

It is a 40-hour, instructor-level course combining classroom instruction, practical deployment work and scenario exercises.

Is the course POST certified and reimbursable?

Yes. The course is California POST certified and listed as Plan IV reimbursable, which covers tuition. Travel and per diem are not reimbursed under Plan IV — confirm eligibility with your agency training manager.

How long is the Less Lethal Instructor Course?

It is a 30-hour, instructor-level course that blends legal standards, platform operation, practical drills and teaching methodology.

Is it AB 48 compliant?

Yes. The course covers AB 48 requirements and compliance for kinetic energy projectiles used in crowd-control situations, including targeting restrictions and documentation.

What does POST Plan IV reimbursement cover?

Plan IV reimburses tuition for eligible POST-certified courses. It does not cover travel or per diem. Your agency training manager can confirm eligibility and submit the request.

How do I register?

Use the contact form or call +1 (928) 614-0964. Our team confirms seat availability, sends registration details and answers Plan IV questions.

Can we host a course at our agency?

Yes. Agencies with a classroom and a suitable outdoor training area can host a session. Visit our Host a Course page or contact us to discuss dates.

Where are you located?

Southwestern Solutions is based in San Diego, California, and delivers courses in San Diego County and at host agencies across California.

[/sws_section] [sws_section][sws_cta ][/sws_section]

Information We Collect

When you submit our contact or registration request form we collect the details you provide: name, agency, email, phone, course of interest and message. Our website may also collect standard technical data such as IP address and browser type through server logs and analytics.

How We Use It

We use your information only to respond to your inquiry, manage course registration, send course-related communications and improve our website. We do not sell your personal information.

Cookies & Analytics

We may use cookies and analytics tools to understand how visitors use the site. You can disable cookies in your browser settings.

Your Rights

California residents may request access to or deletion of their personal information under the CCPA/CPRA. Contact us at info@southwesternsolutions.org.

item.title: AB 48 Explained: What Penal Code 13652 Means for Crowd-Control Training
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Since January 1, 2022, California Penal Code 13652 — added by Assembly Bill 48 — has governed how law enforcement may use kinetic energy projectiles (KEPs) and chemical agents to disperse an assembly, protest or demonstration. For instructors, the law is more than a policy update: it makes training itself a legal prerequisite for deployment.

1. Training Comes First

PC 13652 limits crowd-control use of these tools to officers who have received POST-standard training on their proper use for crowd control. If your agency's instructor pipeline is thin, your pool of officers who may lawfully deploy is thin too.

2. The Threshold for Use

Deployment must be objectively reasonable to defend against a threat to life or serious bodily injury to any person — including officers — or to bring an objectively dangerous and unlawful situation safely and effectively under control.

3. Conditions That Must Be Trained

  • De-escalation and reasonable alternatives attempted when objectively reasonable.
  • Repeated, audible announcements of intent and the type of tool, in languages likely understood.
  • Reasonable effort to distinguish people engaged in violence from those who are not.
  • An objectively reasonable opportunity to disperse.
  • No KEP targeting of the head, neck or other vital organs.
  • No deployment solely for a curfew violation, verbal threat or noncompliance with a directive.
  • Medical aid available or summoned after use.

4. Documentation and Public Reporting

PC 13652.1 requires agencies to publish a summary of each incident in which these tools are used to disperse a crowd. Good reports start in the classroom: instructors should drill documentation alongside tactics.

What This Means for Your Instructors

Instructors must teach the law, the technique and the paperwork as one integrated system. Scenario exercises should include warnings, dispersal time and target discrimination — not just accuracy.

item.title: Chemical Agent Instructor Certification: What a 40-Hour POST Course Covers
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
A chemical agent instructor carries a heavy responsibility: they shape how an entire agency selects, deploys and documents chemical munitions. That is why an instructor-level course looks very different from an end-user class.

Use of Force and Policy Review

Every deployment decision begins with law and policy. A strong course reviews use-of-force standards, your agency's policy language and the specific AB 48 / Penal Code 13652 limits on crowd-control use.

Protective Mask Proficiency

Confidence in the mask is the foundation of everything else. Instructors learn fitting, inspection, clearing and how to run safe confidence exercises for their own students.

Munitions and Deployment Techniques

Students study delivery systems, munition characteristics and environmental factors such as wind, terrain and enclosed spaces — then put that knowledge to work in practical deployments.

Decontamination and Aftercare

Responsible deployment ends with decontamination and medical considerations for both officers and subjects. Instructors learn to teach these procedures as a non-negotiable part of every evolution.

Instruction Techniques

The difference between an operator and an instructor is the ability to transfer skill. Lesson-plan design, safety plans, student evaluation and remediation are core instructor outcomes.

Scenario Exercises

Scenarios tie it all together: warnings, dispersal time, target discrimination, deployment and documentation under realistic pressure.

An instructor course should leave graduates able to teach, evaluate and defend — not just deploy.

item.title: Less Lethal Instructor Training: Building a Defensible KEP Program
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Kinetic energy projectiles (KEPs) give officers a valuable option between verbal commands and higher levels of force. But in California, their use — especially in crowd situations — is closely regulated. A defensible program starts with well-trained instructors.

Pillar 1: Legal Standards

Instructors must be fluent in use-of-force law, agency policy and AB 48 / Penal Code 13652, including the prohibition on aiming KEPs at the head, neck or other vital organs in crowd-control situations.

Pillar 2: Platform and Munition Knowledge

Every launcher and munition has distinct characteristics. Instructors should understand ranges, accuracy, malfunctions and maintenance so they can teach officers to operate safely.

Pillar 3: Precision Under Pressure

Target areas and distance matter. Drills should progress from fundamentals to movement, stress and decision-making — always reinforcing target discrimination.

Pillar 4: Medical and Post-Deployment Procedures

Training should include medical considerations, summoning aid and the steps that follow a deployment.

Pillar 5: Documentation

Thorough, accurate reports protect the public, the officer and the agency — and support the public reporting PC 13652.1 requires for crowd-dispersal incidents.

Why Train Instructors In-House?

Certified in-house instructors let your agency qualify officers on your schedule, keep training consistent with your policy and respond quickly when laws or equipment change.

item.title: POST Plan IV Reimbursement: How Agencies Fund Instructor Courses
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Training budgets are always under pressure. For California agencies, the POST reimbursement plans can make a significant difference — and Plan IV is one of the most commonly used for specialized instructor courses.

What Plan IV Covers

Plan IV reimburses tuition for eligible POST-certified courses. It does not reimburse travel or per diem, so agencies should plan those costs separately.

How to Confirm Eligibility

  • Find the course and presenter in the California POST course catalog.
  • Confirm the specific session is listed as Plan IV reimbursable.
  • Work with your agency training manager to submit the required requests on time.

Ways to Stretch Your Budget

  • Train instructors, not just users. One certified instructor can train many officers in-house.
  • Host a course. Hosting reduces travel for your own officers. See our Host a Course page.
  • Plan ahead. Instructor courses fill quickly — reserving early protects your training calendar.

Southwestern Solutions Courses

Our Chemical Agent Instructor Course and Less Lethal Instructor Course are POST certified and listed as Plan IV reimbursable. Questions? Contact our team.

Reimbursement rules are set by California POST and may change. Always confirm current policies with POST and your agency.

item.title: Decontamination and Aftercare After Chemical Agent Deployment
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Chemical agents are effective precisely because they are uncomfortable. That makes decontamination and aftercare a core part of responsible use — for subjects, bystanders and officers alike.

Make Aftercare Part of the Plan

Deployment plans should identify how and where decontamination will occur and how medical aid will be summoned, before any munition is used. California's PC 13652 also emphasizes the availability of medical aid after crowd-control deployments.

Officer Decontamination

Officers and instructors are exposed repeatedly during training. Lesson plans should include clear procedures for clearing masks, removing contaminated equipment and caring for exposed skin and eyes according to agency and manufacturer guidance.

Subject Care

Follow your agency's policy and medical guidance for exposed subjects, monitor for medical distress and summon medical personnel when indicated.

Equipment and Facility Considerations

Contaminated gear, vehicles and indoor spaces require attention. Instructors should teach how to handle and clean equipment and how to ventilate affected areas according to manufacturer guidance.

Document Everything

Record the decontamination steps taken, medical aid provided and any complaints of injury. Complete documentation supports transparency and required public reporting.

Teach decontamination with the same seriousness as deployment — because the public judges both.

item.title: Train-the-Trainer: Why In-House Instructors Strengthen Accountability
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Every agency faces the same challenge: keep officers proficient, compliant and confident while budgets and schedules stay tight. A train-the-trainer model solves much of that problem.

Consistency

In-house instructors teach to your policy, your equipment and your community. That consistency makes training records easier to defend and performance easier to evaluate.

Speed

When laws like AB 48 change, certified instructors can update lesson plans and retrain officers quickly — without waiting for outside course availability.

Cost Control

One instructor seat can translate into training for an entire shift, unit or department. Combined with POST Plan IV tuition reimbursement, the return on investment is substantial.

Culture and Credibility

Officers respond to instructors they know and respect. Peer instructors with real operational experience build buy-in that outside lectures rarely achieve.

Documentation

Certified instructors understand what must be recorded — attendance, objectives, proficiency and remediation — creating a training record that supports accountability.
